subject: Clarify: Confirmation of Model Training Exclusion & Retention Detail for Finovate POC
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@finovate.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajeev Singh <rajeev.s@finovate.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Quick confirmation: Do you train on customer data? + retention questions

Hi Lukas,

We're kicking off the POC with Redwood next week and our security team has two quick asks before we start routing production test traffic:

1) A plain-language confirmation that Redwood will not use Finovate customer content to train or improve general models (including via mixed-batch telemetry).
2) A clear timeline for retention and deletion for request logs, KV cache snapshots, debug snapshots, and periodic backups — specifically: what is the default retention, and what are the deletion guarantees for "erase on request" customers?

Can you point us to a canonical statement and any artifacts (attestation/letter) we can include with our vendor assessment? If there are operational caveats (e.g., aggregated telemetry), please spell them out — we need to know what we can represent to our audit team.

Thanks,
Ellen
Security Operations
Finovate

From: lukas_meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: Do you train on customer data? + retention questions

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer upfront: Redwood does not train public or internal model-weight updates on customer request/response data for hosted or dedicated customers by default. We commit in writing to a "no-training" clause for customers who opt into the non-training SLA (DOC attached).

Key operational details and caveats (summary):
- Model training: Customer payloads are not used to update model weights or for continued pretraining/fine-tuning unless a customer explicitly opts into a research program or signs a separate data-sharing consent.
- Aggregated telemetry: We collect high-level telemetry (aggregate latency histograms, error rates, token counts) to operate the service. These metrics are aggregated and cannot be reconstructed into customer messages.
- Caching & KV snapshots: For performance we maintain ephemeral KV cache and prefix caches on serving nodes. These caches are not persisted to long-term model training stores. Where snapshots are persisted (debug or replay for incident analysis) they are covered by retention rules and customer erase requests.
- Backups & snapshots: Regular backups of metadata and logs exist for reliability; backups are tombstoned and subject to automated expiration/retention windows (default 90 days for non-enterprise hosted).
- Erase-on-request: We have an erase playbook — request receipt, tombstone markers, background eviction of caches, and confirmation when snapshots and backups are processed by retention engines. SLA for deletion confirmation varies by deployment: hosted (30 days), dedicated with reserved commit (14 days), private (customer-managed; Redwood provides tooling and playbook).

I'll loop in Mina (Privacy) and Priyom (Legal/Contracts) for any formal attestation and the written no-train committment. I've attached a short committment doc and a retention matrix specific to Finovate's questions.

Next steps:
- Mina to confirm wording for the attestation.
- Priyom to confirm delete SLA language and any procurement clause suggestions.
- If helpful, we can arrange a 30-min call with our infra lead to walk through caching lifecycle and backup deletion mechanics.

Best,
Lukas Meyer

Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: Do you train on customer data? + retention questions

Hi Ellen —

Following up with the attestation language and a few operational clarifications for the audit team:

1) Attestation excerpt (for vendor file): "Redwood Inference confirms that, by default, customer request/response content is not used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update Redwood models or derivative models. Any use of customer data for model development requires explicit, documented consent and a separate contract amendment."

2) Deletion lifecycle details (operational):
- Request logs (API request/response bodies): default retention 30 days for hosted; deletion-on-request processed within 30 days. For Dedicated customers we can contract to 14-day processing and for Private deployments deletion is customer-controlled.
- KV cache snapshots: ephemeral (kept only in memory on serving nodes). For debug snapshots we take minimal persisted captures only when troubleshooting; those are stored encrypted and deleted per the retention matrix.
- Backups & cold storage: backups are rotated and encrypted; we apply tombstones and retention sweeps — final purge may take an additional window (up to 90 days in edge cases where legal holds or nested backup chains exist).
- Audit logs & evidence: We can provide time-stamped confirmation and a deletion certificate for erase requests once the retention engine completes purging across primary storage and Glacier-style backups.

3) Telemetry and ML signals: We may use aggregated, de-identified signals (e.g., per-model latency distributions, token usage percentiles) for platform optimization. These are non-reversible and excluded from any training corpus.

4) Exceptions & research opt-in: We maintain a documented process for customers that wish to opt into research/model improvement programs — requires opt-in, explicit data scope, and separate legal approval.

I've attached the short attestation as a signed PDF and the retention matrix for Finovate-specific defaults; Priyom, please add procurement-friendly clause language for the SOW.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Erase-on-request will be processed per the retention matrix provided; confirmation certificates can be provided upon request."
